prompt:
Create one new finished 2D painted fantasy merchant-location environment concept, landscape 16:9, using the supplied images as ART DIRECTION REFERENCES ONLY. Reference 1 defines the environment painting, three-quarter elevated camera, materials and light. Reference 2 defines chunky sculpted silhouettes, faceted weathered grey stone, soft moss and aged bronze; DO NOT depict its golem or any other character. The result must be a NEW SHOP MAP with its own architecture and layout, not the reference library with a few objects added. Match the confident dark drawn contours, broad painterly shaded color planes, handmade asymmetrical proportions, blue-slate masonry, olive moss, gnarled roots, oxidized bronze fittings, restrained turquoise magic and intimate amber candlelight. The world feels ancient, magical, inhabited and welcoming, with believable material wear. A beautiful illustrated RPG background with excellent readability at gameplay scale, neither photorealistic nor a generic glossy 3D render. Elevated three-quarter game camera, looking down enough to read all counters and floor paths, coherent parallel floor axes, no visible sky or horizon. Full-bleed environment fills the landscape frame, not an isolated floating miniature. Design for future point-and-click shopping: broad connected dry stone walkways from the lower foreground to every counter; 40 to 50 percent visually quiet walking and approach space; clearly separated merchandise silhouettes; unobstructed empty floor behind counters for future shopkeeper placement. Make about four potential object-interaction destinations visually distinct, with gentle local lighting rather than UI effects. Tall structures remain along back and sides, foreground objects low and cropped only at the frame edges. Every counter has an accessible customer side. Low overall clutter, detail concentrated in useful clusters, strongly readable shape hierarchy. NO people, NO humanoids, NO golems, NO creatures, NO character statues, NO faces, NO UI, NO labels, NO readable text, NO prices, NO icons, NO cursor, NO selection outline, NO grid, NO watermark, NO collage or split panels. No huge luminous portal that competes with the merchandise. Render one complete coherent scene.

VARIANT A — THE ARCHIVE RELIC SHOP. An intimate rectangular chamber in the same ancient library complex as reference 1, now a carefully organized antiquarian shop. A solid dark oak L-shaped counter sits along the upper-right wall, its lower customer side fully visible, with broad empty standing space behind it. Upper-left wall has tall recessed bookshelves between massive mossy blue-grey stone piers. Three LOW, generously separated merchandise displays around the outer edges: one open jewel-bound grimoire on a slanted reading stand at left-middle; one open brass-inlaid chest holding an ancient key at right-middle; one faceted turquoise crystal in a bronze mount on a low square pedestal near the back-left. A broad gently curving uninterrupted floor aisle enters from bottom-center and connects every display to the counter. Warm clusters of candles illuminate parchment, polished wood and brass. A tiny recessed cyan crystal lamp in a rear arch gives cool depth, not a portal. Roots and one motionless bronze wheel decorate the distant wall. Restrained palette of midnight blue, olive, amber and cyan; the most intimate and bookish of the three concepts. No bodies, mannequins or suits of armor. The central aisle is quiet, dry and clear. Present as a compelling premium game environment painting.
